the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
demographic: relating to the structure of a population
The company studied demographic trends before opening a new store.
navigating: finding a way through a difficult situation or place
việc xoay xở, tìm đường qua
She spent months navigating the complicated visa application process.
economic: relating to trade, industry, and the management of money
The government announced new economic reforms to boost growth.
impact: a powerful effect or the force of one object hitting another
The new policy had a huge impact on small businesses.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
aging: The country's aging workforce worries many economists.
populations: groups of people, animals, or organisms living in an area
Wildlife populations in the region have declined sharply since the drought.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
east: the direction from which the sun rises
The hotel windows face east, so the sunrise wakes us early.
asia: the largest continent, covering much of the eastern hemisphere
The company plans to expand its business across Southeast Asia next year.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
southern: located in or relating to the south of an area
Southern regions of the country tend to have warmer winters.
europe: a continent made up of many countries, including France and Germany
Roads were built across Europe long before cars existed.
fertility: the ability to produce children, young, or crops
Fertility rates have fallen in many developed countries.
rates: speeds at which things happen, or fixed prices or measures
Interest rates rose sharply after the central bank's announcement.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
challenging: difficult in a way that tests one's ability or determination
The team completed the project despite challenging weather conditions.
growth: the process of increasing, or a layer that has developed
Algal growth on the pond's surface blocked most of the sunlight.
models: simplified representations of something, used to explain or predict it
Scientists use climate models to forecast future temperature changes.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
social: relating to society or to spending time with other people
She enjoys an active social life with many close friends.
throughout: all the way through a period of time or place
Cheap substitutes existed throughout, and they were widely used.
twentieth: coming after the nineteenth in a sequence; relating to the 1900s
For most of the twentieth century, engineers responded by building bigger pipes.
century: a period of one hundred years
The tradition has been passed down for more than a century.
global: relating to the whole world; worldwide
Climate change is a global problem requiring international cooperation.
discourse: communication or debate about a topic, spoken or written
Climate change has become a central topic in public discourse.
was: past tense of 'be', used for the first/third person singular
Half an hour after a lesson ends, much of what was said is already gone.
consumed: used up, ate, or experienced something completely
The whole cake was consumed within minutes of the party starting.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
over: during the whole of a period of time; more than
Prices have risen steadily over the past five years.
predictions: statements about what will happen in the future
The company's predictions about future sales were far too optimistic.
warned: told someone about a possible danger or problem
Meteorologists warned that light winds could make temperatures feel higher.
resource: something that can be used to achieve a purpose
Fresh water is becoming a scarce resource in many regions.
exhaustion: After the long hike, exhaustion finally caught up with them.
famine: an extreme shortage of food affecting a large population
The drought led to a severe famine across the region.
collapse: a sudden failure or breakdown of something
Poor management led to the collapse of the company.
under: in a position below something; less than
A supermarket loaf can be mixed, risen and baked in under three hours.
weight: how heavy something is; a heavy object
That turn moves the wheels back underneath the falling weight of the rider.
human: relating to or characteristic of people
con người, thuộc về con người
The robot cannot yet match human judgment in complex situations.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
stunning: The view from the summit was absolutely stunning at sunrise.
historical: relating to history or past events
The museum displays several historical documents from the war.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
surplus: an amount left over after needs have been met
The farm sold its grain surplus at the local market each autumn.
beings: living creatures, especially in the phrase 'human beings'
The novel explores what makes beings from different worlds seem alike.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
unprecedented: never having happened or existed before
The region experienced unprecedented flooding this year.
births: events of babies being born, counted over time
The clinic recorded a rise in births during the spring months.
nations: large bodies of people united by common government, history or culture
Delegates from over a hundred nations attended the climate summit.
such: of the type already mentioned or described
Such behaviour will not be tolerated in the workplace.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
south: the direction that is opposite to north
They drove south for six hours to reach the coast.
korea: a country in East Asia, divided into North and South
Korea has invested heavily in electronics manufacturing since the 1980s.
japan: a country in East Asia made up of many islands
Japan is known for its advanced technology and unique culture.
italy: Papermaking spread quickly through northern Italy in the 13th century.
increasingly: more and more as time goes on
Remote work has become increasingly common since the pandemic.
china: a large country in East Asia
China shares borders with more than a dozen neighbouring countries.
total: the whole amount of something added together
The same amount of water arrives faster, so the peak flow is higher even though the total is unchanged.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
well: in a good or satisfactory way
The bicycle still balanced perfectly well even with the gyroscopic effect cancelled out.
below: at or to a lower position than something
The valley lay below, hidden beneath a thick layer of morning fog.
replacement: a person or thing that takes the place of another
Finding a replacement for the retiring manager took months.
threshold: Falling below the demographic replacement threshold triggers long-term population decline.
ngưỡng cửa / mức giới hạn tới hạn
children: plural of child; young human beings
The park was full of children playing after school.
per: The hotel charges eighty dollars per night for a standard room.
woman: A woman sets out plastic stools and a pot of noodle soup each morning.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
structural: relating to the way something is built or organised
Engineers found a structural weakness in the old bridge.
burgeoning: The city's burgeoning tech industry has attracted thousands of young workers.
cohort: The millennial cohort faces housing cost burdens distinct from preceding generations.
nhóm thuần tập / nhóm người cùng độ tuổi
elderly: Volunteers deliver meals to elderly residents living alone.
retirees: people who have stopped working, usually due to age
Retirees make up a growing share of the population.
supported: backed up or confirmed by evidence; given help
được ủng hộ, có căn cứ
Her claim was well supported by several independent studies.
shrinking: becoming smaller in size or amount
The town's population has been shrinking for the past decade.
workers: people who do a job, especially manual or paid work
Night workers face a harder version of the same problem.
strain: a particular type of an organism, such as a virus or bacterium
Scientists identified a new strain of the flu virus this winter.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
pension: a regular income paid to someone after they retire
She has relied on a small pension since retiring last year.
funds: The trust funds scholarships for students from low-income families.
healthcare: services provided to maintain or improve health
Access to affordable healthcare remains uneven in rural areas.
infrastructure: the basic physical systems a country needs, such as roads and power
The government plans to invest more in rural infrastructure this year.
chronic: persisting for a long time; long-lasting, especially of an illness
Chronic back pain forced him to change careers.
stagnation: Deflationary pressures and demographic shrinking compound long-term economic stagnation.
conundrum: Financing eldercare without overburdening younger workers is a formidable policy conundrum.
